problem.passage:
Text 1
Astronomers analyzing data from a newly launched space telescope argue that the unusual chemical signatures detected in a distant exoplanet's atmosphere are best explained by volcanic activity on the planet's surface. The relative abundance of sulfur compounds, they note, closely matches patterns produced by volcanic outgassing observed on rocky planets within our own solar system. Because no other atmospheric process known to occur on such planets produces this particular combination of gases in these proportions, the researchers conclude that active volcanism offers the most plausible explanation currently available.

Text 2
A separate team analyzing the same telescope data proposes that the sulfur compounds could instead result from chemical reactions between the atmosphere and a subsurface ocean rich in dissolved minerals. Laboratory simulations replicating the exoplanet's estimated temperature and pressure conditions produced similar gas ratios without requiring any volcanic activity at all. This team acknowledges that volcanism remains possible but argues that the ocean-based mechanism should not be dismissed, since it independently reproduces the same chemical signatures observed by the telescope.

problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 that no other atmospheric process produces the observed combination of gases in these proportions?
options: By presenting laboratory results showing that ocean-atmosphere chemical reactions can independently reproduce similar gas ratios without volcanism
By agreeing that volcanic outgassing is the only process capable of producing the observed sulfur compound ratios
By suggesting that the sulfur compound ratios could also be explained by atmospheric processes unrelated to either volcanism or subsurface ocean chemistry
By suggesting that both volcanic activity and ocean-atmosphere reactions might be occurring simultaneously, making it impossible to isolate a single cause
problem.explanation: Text 2는 지하 해양과 대기 사이의 화학 반응을 재현한 실험실 시뮬레이션이 화산 활동 없이도 관측된 것과 유사한 기체 비율을 만들어냈다고 설명한다. 이는 화산 활동만이 이 조합의 기체를 만들 수 있는 유일한 과정이라는 Text 1의 주장에 대한 구체적인 반례를 제시하는 것이다. Text 2는 화산 활동의 가능성 자체를 부정하지는 않지만, 대안적 메커니즘도 배제해서는 안 된다고 주장한다. 따라서 정답은 A이다. B는 Text 1의 입장을 그대로 반복한 것으로 Text 2의 반박 취지와 반대된다. C는 지문에서 실제로는 황 화합물이 알려진 화학적 과정(해양 반응)과 일치한다고 설명한 것과 정반대다. D는 지문에 없는 내용으로, 두 팀이 다른 결론에 도달했다고 해서 데이터 자체에 결함이 있다고 주장하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Text 2 describes laboratory simulations that replicated the exoplanet's estimated temperature and pressure conditions and produced gas ratios similar to those observed, without requiring volcanic activity. This provides a concrete counterexample to Text 1's claim that volcanism is the only process capable of producing this combination of gases. Text 2 does not deny volcanism is possible but argues the ocean-based mechanism should not be dismissed. So the correct answer is A. Option B simply restates Text 1's position, contradicting Text 2's rebuttal. Option C contradicts the text, since the sulfur compounds are shown to be consistent with a known chemical process (ocean reactions). Option D is unsupported by the text, which never suggests the data itself is flawed. Option E contradicts Text 2's actual argument, which relies on the plausibility of a subsurface ocean.

problem.evidenceTarget: Text 2는 화산 활동만이 관측된 황 화합물 비율을 설명할 수 있다는 Text 1의 주장에 대해, 실험실 시뮬레이션을 통해 해양-대기 반응도 동일한 기체 비율을 화산 활동 없이 재현할 수 있음을 제시하며 반박한다.
problem.evidenceSpan: Laboratory simulations replicating the exoplanet's estimated temperature and pressure conditions produced similar gas ratios without requiring any volcanic activity at all
problem.answerRationale: Text 2는 다른 메커니즘(해양-광물 반응)이 동일한 화학적 결과를 독립적으로 재현했다는 실험 증거를 제시함으로써, 화산 활동이 유일한 설명이라는 Text 1의 주장에 대안을 제공한다.

difficultyReasons: Text 2의 핵심 주장(실험실 시뮬레이션으로 동일 비율 재현)을 그대로 확인하면 되는 1단계 추론
정답과 오답 간 표현 차이가 뚜렷해 텍스트를 한 번만 읽어도 구분 가능
